lt.title: Load test: zero oversell
lt.lead: Fire hundreds of simultaneous booking requests at a room with only a few units left, then check the database itself, not the responses.
lt.bypassHint: Skips the in-memory sold-out shield, so every request contends for the database row lock.
lt.verdictLine: {granted} of {expected} expected bookings granted out of {n} simultaneous requests; {rej} correctly rejected.
lt.chartLabel: Chart of requests answered over time
lt.check.no_oversell.why: booked + held never exceeds total, anywhere in the database.
lt.check.exactly_free_units_granted: Exactly the free units were granted
lt.check.exactly_free_units_granted.why: Not one more, not one fewer.
lt.check.no_request_granted_twice.why: Retries with the same idempotency key never created a second hold.
lt.check.counters_reconcile: Counters reconcile with the holds table
lt.check.counters_reconcile.why: held_units equals the sum of active holds: no unit was lost or double-counted.
lt.check.db_check_never_fired: The database safety net never fired
lt.check.db_check_never_fired.why: The application logic did the work; the CHECK constraint was never needed.
lt.check.no_transport_or_server_errors.w: Every request got a clean answer: granted or sold out.
lt.evLock: database sessions blocked on the row lock at once
lt.evNet: times the DB safety net had to fire
lt.evOversold: oversold rows in the whole database
lt.shieldOn: The in-memory sold-out shield was on, so it queued requests before the database. Turn on “Attack the database directly” to test the row lock itself.
lt.cleanup: Test holds were released afterwards ({n}); the room is back as it was.
lt.inv.held_drift: rows where held ≠ sum of active holds
lt.inv.booked_drift: rows where booked ≠ sum of confirmed items
failure.hold_expired: The hold expired before checkout finished
lt.dupExplain: Each request was sent {d}× with the same idempotency key. {n} duplicate attempt(s) got the same booking back instead of creating another one, so “Granted” counts distinct bookings, not attempts.

ops.title: Operations dashboard
ops.sub: Live from the database, refreshed every 2 seconds
ops.invariantsWhy: Checked straight from the tables: nothing oversold, no negative counters, and held and booked units equal the holds and bookings behind them.
ops.activityNote: Holds and bookings come from the database (last hour). Rejected attempts are kept in memory since the last server start.
ops.noActivity: No activity in the last hour — reserve a room as a traveller.
ops.resetBody: This releases every active hold and cancels every confirmed booking that the 10 demo users made in the app, returning the stock. Nothing is deleted and the provided seed data is not touched.
search.connectionsNote: Two flights booked together: both seats are held at once, so you never end up with only one leg. The connection is at least an hour long.
